findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification
findings.body: Password verification above is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is non-empty, while the new backup-code branch only checks credentials.backupCode and does not itself verify the password. A crafted credentials request containing a valid backup code plus any dummy totpCode therefore authenticates without knowing the account password. A backup code is meant to replace only the TOTP second factor, so this reduces account login to possession of a single long-lived backup code.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is not atomic, allowing concurrent replay
findings.body: The code reads the encrypted backup-code array, checks indexOf, and later writes back the same array with one entry nulled. Two concurrent login attempts using the same code can both read the original array and pass the check before either update completes, so a supposedly single-use backup code can establish multiple sessions. Consumption needs an atomic/transactional update or locking to guarantee single use.

findings.title: Backup-code comparison does not normalize case or surrounding whitespace
findings.body: Generated codes are lowercase hex and are displayed/downloaded in XXXXX-XXXXX form, but verification only removes hyphens. A user who transcribes or pastes the correct code with uppercase A-F letters, or with surrounding whitespace, is rejected with IncorrectBackupCode. The same normalization issue exists in the disable endpoint, so valid backup-code holders can be locked out of both login and disabling 2FA.

findings.title: Users who enabled 2FA before this feature can never obtain backup codes
findings.body: The migration adds backupCodes as null for existing users, and setup returns TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled for anyone with twoFactorEnabled set. Such users are still offered the Lost access flow, receive MissingBackupCodes, and are told to generate codes in settings, but there is no settings action to generate or regenerate backup codes without first disabling 2FA with a working authenticator. That makes the recovery path unusable for the entire pre-existing 2FA user base.

findings.title: No test exercises backup-code login, single-use consumption, or disabling with a backup code
findings.body: The added e2e coverage only checks that the download and copy buttons exist/work during setup in the disable test. As the TODO acknowledges, nothing tests logging in with a backup code, rejecting an incorrect code, rejecting reuse of a consumed code, handling missing codes for legacy users, or disabling 2FA with a backup code. These are security-critical server paths in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts and can regress without any test failing.

findings.title: Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard tab order globally
findings.body: Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide password button in the shared PasswordField makes that control unreachable by keyboard for every password field in the app, not just the 2FA setup form. Keyboard-only users can no longer toggle password visibility, an accessibility regression unrelated to backup codes.
